title: Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
author: Zhiyu
excerpt: In the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang, three passages discuss the compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, and they are now widely cited as “ironclad proof” that he opposed compiling that sutra. The facts, however, are the very opposite: in these three passages Master Yinguang not only never said the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled, but in fact said it could.

inline.s: In the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang (Yinguang fashi wenchao), three passages discuss the compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, and they are now widely cited as
“ironclad proof”
that Master Yinguang opposed compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
Yet the facts are exactly the opposite.
In these three passages,
Master Yinguang
not only never said
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled;
on the contrary,
he said the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could be compiled
Our analysis follows.
(From
the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang
, the third letter in reply to the layman Gao Shaolin
Master Yinguang said:

“The Amitābha Sutra, the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, and the Sutra on the Contemplation of Amitāyus Buddha — also called the Sutra of Sixteen Contemplations — are together called the Three Pure Land Sutras; with the addition of the chapter on the Practices and Vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, they are called the Four Pure Land Sutras. In the catalogue there is a single-volume edition of the Four Pure Land Sutras; its Sutra of Immeasurable Life was abridged by Wei Chengguan, who then supplemented it from other sutras
(that is, sutras other than the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
. Although the principle is beneficial, the actual result is gravely mistaken, and it must not be followed
in any future compilation of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, one must never follow his approach)
[Analysis] This teaching of Master Yinguang means: Wei Chengguan’s compiled edition (the “Wei Compilation” for short) should not
draw on other sutras
(sutras other than the original translations of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
to supplement it
. This only says that Wei Chengguan’s method of compilation was improper;
it never says
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled
! Moreover, Master Yinguang said:
“Although the principle is beneficial, the actual result is gravely mistaken, and it must not be followed
in any future compilation of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, one must never follow his approach)
This also shows:
Master Yinguang held that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could be compiled!
(From the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang, the second letter in reply to a certain layman of Yongjia)

This letter was written by Master Yinguang in reply to a request from a certain layman of Yongjia (Zhou Mengyou), who had praised the book The Essence of Amitābha as “heartfelt and earnest” and hoped the Master would promote its circulation. In the letter, Master Yinguang clearly states that The Essence of Amitābha must not be circulated, because it
“alters the sutra and denounces the ancients”

. “Altering the sutra” refers to the book’s intent to replace the Sutra of Immeasurable Life as translated by Saṃghavarman with the “Wei Compilation”; “denouncing the ancients” refers to the book’s censure of such patriarchs as Master Feixi, Master Lianchi, and Master Ouyi.
Master Yinguang said:

“Circulating the Buddha-dharma is by no means an easy matter. Translating sutras and treatises is never to be undertaken casually; hence within a translation assembly there are the chief translator, the interpreters, the verifiers of meaning, and the polishers of prose. How could one dare to disseminate the Buddha’s sutras by shaping them according to one’s own judgment?
[Analysis] The above concerns the question of circulating the Buddha’s sutras; but a compiled edition is not a sutra, and so it does not fall within this category.

Wang Longshu’s Larger Amitābha Sutra, from the Song dynasty to the end of the Ming, was received and upheld by many people. Because Yunqi [Master Lianchi] found that it still contained improprieties, it gradually fell into oblivion thereafter. Wei Chengguan’s learning is inferior to Longshu’s, yet he presumed even more upon himself than Longshu did. To work by following another’s track makes the task easy; how could Chengguan surpass Longshu? Since Master Lianchi would not circulate Wang’s edition
, how dare we
(we of this generation)

circulate Wei’s edition, thereby opening the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddha’s sutras and giving fodder to those who denounce the Buddha, who would claim that the Buddhist sutras are all later fabrications and were not truly translated from the land of the Buddha.

[Analysis] This passage says: Although Wang Longshu’s compiled edition, the Larger Amitābha Sutra (the “Wang Compilation” for short), was received and upheld by many from the Song dynasty to the end of the Ming, it still contained improprieties, and so Master Lianchi no longer circulated it. Since Wei Chengguan’s compilation does not even measure up to the “Wang Compilation,” it likewise ought not to be circulated.
Please note in particular:
Master Yinguang said that the “Wang Compilation” had improprieties, and that the “Wei Compilation” did not even measure up to it.
He did not say that Wang Longshu and Wei Chengguan should never have compiled at all!
Master Yinguang’s words,

“How dare we circulate Wei’s edition, thereby opening the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddha’s sutras and giving fodder to those who denounce the Buddha, who would claim that the Buddhist sutras are all later fabrications and were not truly translated from the land of the Buddha,”

are a criticism aimed at those who circulate the “Wei Compilation” as if it were a sutra (without labeling it as a compiled edition). They also sound a warning for the circulation of compiled editions:
a compiled edition is a compiled edition, not a sutra. When circulating a compiled edition, one must clearly label it as a compiled edition
Consider this: if a compiled edition already bore the words “compiled edition” clearly on its cover, how could it

“open the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddha’s sutras and give fodder to those who denounce the Buddha, who would claim that the Buddhist sutras are all later fabrications and were not truly translated from the land of the Buddha”
For a compiled edition is simply not a sutra, and so it can hardly be spoken of as recklessly altering or fabricating the Buddha’s sutras.
Master Lianchi did not circulate the “Wang Compilation” because it was a compiled edition, but because it contained
improprieties.
Moreover, even as Master Lianchi regretfully pointed out its improprieties, he still praised it:
“Truly, it has rendered great service to the Pure Land!”
Master Lianchi said:
“The layman’s compiling of the four translations
(layman Wang Longshu’s compilation of the four original translations)
, the wording concise yet the meaning complete, the expression smooth yet the principle clear.
Truly, it has rendered great service to the Pure Land! It is a pity
that it still contains much that is unsettled
it is a pity
that it still contains much that is improper)
(Daily Recitation of the Scriptures)
In this passage,
Master Yinguang
never said
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled!
Rather, he said that Wei Chengguan compiled it poorly, and that it must not be circulated as a sutra (without labeling it a compiled edition).
The two passages that follow concern the matter of The Essence of Amitābha.
“Yet this sutra and this treatise, if read by a true practitioner of superior capacity, can also be of great benefit.

For one then takes only their benefit without being tainted by their flaws. But if a person of inferior capacity reads them, before gaining the benefit he first suffers harm — for he merely imitates their
alteration of the sutra and denunciation of the ancients
— a fault
(“altering the sutra” refers to replacing the Sutra of Immeasurable Life translated by Saṃghavarman with the “Wei Compilation”; “denouncing the ancients” refers to how
Wang Gengxin, in
The Essence of Amitābha, censures such patriarchs as Master Feixi, Master Lianchi, and Master Ouyi; “fault (qiān)” means offense or transgression)
, and fails to emulate its direct, focused practice
(the “direct, focused practice” refers to the Buddha-name recitation, retreat recitation, and realization of the buddhānusmṛti samādhi taught in The Essence of Amitābha)
[This sutra and this treatise]
“This sutra”
refers to Wei Chengguan’s compiled edition; “this treatise” refers to Wang Gengxin’s “Essence.” The book The Essence of Amitābha consists of two main parts
the first part is
Wei Chengguan’s compiled edition; the second part is Wang Gengxin’s “Essence.”
[Altering the sutra] The Essence of Amitābha says that the five original translations
“are none of them good editions”
. It especially criticizes the Sutra of Immeasurable Life translated by Saṃghavarman, saying of it:

“repetitive and verbose … therefore the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, to this day, is not included in the daily recitation of the monasteries. Thus the great vow of our Buddha, the World-Honored One — the cause encompassing the ocean of fruition, the fruition penetrating the source of the cause — is not made manifest
(“zhang” here has the ancient meaning of “to make manifest”)
in the world. Is this not a great regret for the scriptural teaching of the Pure Land!”
And it lavishly praises the “Wei Compilation” as
“the crown
(of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
of this sutra”
, seeking to replace Saṃghavarman’s translation with the “Wei Compilation.” [Denouncing the ancients] In the earlier part of this letter, Master Yinguang wrote:
“As for censuring Zige
(Master Feixi)
, Yunqi
(Master Lianchi)
, Ouyi and the rest — this only reveals how little he has seen and heard.”
[Analysis] This passage says:
Although the book The Essence of Amitābha is of great benefit to persons of superior capacity, for persons of inferior capacity it brings harm before benefit is gained.

One teaches by observing the capacities of beings, and prescribes the medicine according to the illness. Teaching that does not suit the capacity is just like medicine that does not match the illness. How dare one take the one or two worthwhile points
(the “one or two worthwhile points” refers to the Buddha-name recitation, retreat recitation, and realization of the buddhānusmṛti samādhi taught in The Essence of Amitābha)
and then circulate it everywhere
(this means: The Essence of Amitābha should not be circulated everywhere)

, thereby bequeathing fault and transgression to persons of inferior capacity (this refers to the fact that if a true cultivator of superior capacity reads The Essence of Amitābha, it is of great benefit; but if a person of inferior capacity reads it, he will be misled by its altering the sutra and denouncing the ancients)
[Analysis]
This passage says: The Essence of Amitābha should not be circulated everywhere, lest it mislead persons of inferior capacity.
Summary:
In the four passages above,
Master Yinguang
never said
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled!
(From
the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang
, the third letter in reply to the layman Wang Zili)
In the following letter, Master Yinguang chiefly clarifies the error of Wang Longshu’s compiled edition,
and the reason for it:

his rigidly clinging to the view that the three grades spoken of in the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades spoken of in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha.
This error (that among the three grades of rebirth, only the middle grade gives rise to the bodhi mind) was pointed out by Master Lianchi, but he did not specifically explain that it stemmed from
“rigidly clinging to the notion that the three grades are the nine grades”
; hence Master Yinguang, in this letter, clarifies the reason for it.
At the end of the letter, Master Yinguang writes in summary:
“I write this partly to show the difficulty of compiling, and partly to put an end to the presumptions of later generations

(in writing the above, I wish on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling, and on the other to put an end to the later generations’ presumptuous clinging to the view that ‘the three grades are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades’)
He also points out that Wei Moshen was bold but crude, and that his compiled edition (the “Wei Compilation”) is not worthy to be taken as a model (
“not fit to serve as a model”
[Though Master Lianchi pointed it out, he did not explain it specifically …] Master Lianchi’s Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra says:
“Therein
(in Wang Longshu’s compiled edition)
the selecting and discarding of the old text
(the selecting and discarding of the sutra text of the original translations)
is also not without omissions. For instance, regarding the rebirth of the three grades, the Wei translation
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)

says in each case ‘give rise to the bodhi mind,’ yet Master Wang has only the middle grade giving rise to the bodhi mind, says of the lower grade that it does not give rise to it, and of the upper grade says nothing at all — thus the high and low lose their proper order. Moreover, the abundant good roots in the text all lie in giving rise to the bodhi mind. Yet although the three grades differ, the single giving rise to the mind is precisely the essential point of rebirth, and it has instead been omitted — hence my saying it is not without omissions.”
[Hence Master Yinguang, in this letter, clarifies the reason for it]

In the original translations of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, all three grades — upper, middle, and lower — give rise to the bodhi mind, and so all are good people. Wang Longshu, however, wrongly held that the upper, middle, and lower grades of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha. And in the Contemplation Sutra, the lower three grades are all evil people. He therefore reasoned: since the lower grade consists of evil people, how could evil people give rise to the bodhi mind? Thus the “Wang Compilation” says:
“Those born in the lower grade cannot perform any merits,
and do not give rise to the supreme bodhi mind
This is an error of principle. Hence Master Yinguang, in this letter, criticizes it:
Therefore, to take the lower grade as the lower three grades is a grave error.

Hence he does not say of the upper grade that it gives rise to the bodhi mind, says of the middle grade that it does give rise to it, and says of the lower grade that it does not give rise to it. Yet the three grades of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life all give rise to the bodhi mind. The layman Wang thought: the lower grade is burdened with grave offenses, how could it give rise to the bodhi mind? He did not consider that the lower grade is never once said to have committed any misdeeds — they are good people, fit only to be the middle grade of the nine grades.
He insisted on turning the lower grade into the lower grade
(this is “making trouble out of nothing”)
, contrary to the sutra and lacking in principle — this amounts to altering the sutra at will, and the error is great.”

[[And on the other hand, to put an end to the later generations’ presumptuous clinging to the view that ‘the three grades are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades’] In fact, before Master Yinguang’s letter, people who had not deeply studied Master Lianchi’s teaching all took it for granted that the three grades were the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades. And even after the letter was published, many who had not read this teaching of Master Yinguang still took it for granted that the three grades were the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades.
[[The “Wei Compilation” is not worthy to serve as a model] Master Yinguang said:
“In the catalogue there is a single-volume edition of the Four Pure Land Sutras; its Sutra of Immeasurable Life was abridged by Wei Chengguan, who then supplemented it from other sutras
(that is, sutras other than the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
. Although the principle is beneficial, the actual result is gravely mistaken, and it must not be followed
(in any future compilation of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, one must never follow his approach)
(From the Collected Writings of Master Yinguang, the third letter in reply to the layman Gao Shaolin)
Master Yinguang said:

“In the Sutra of Immeasurable Life there are three grades; in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha there are nine grades. The lower three grades are all people who have created evil karma, and who attain rebirth only because at the end of life they meet a good spiritual friend who teaches them to recite the Buddha’s name.
Wang Longshu
rigidly clings to the notion that the three grades are the nine grades
(rigidly clinging to the view that the three grades spoken of in the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are the nine grades spoken of in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha, namely
the upper three, middle three, and lower three grades among them
, and this is the root of his error.

Therefore, to take the lower grade as the lower three grades is a grave error. Hence he does not say of the upper grade that it gives rise to the bodhi mind, says of the middle grade that it does give rise to it, and says of the lower grade that it does not give rise to it. Yet the three grades of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life all give rise to the bodhi mind. The layman Wang thought: the lower grade is burdened with grave offenses, how could it give rise to the bodhi mind? He did not consider that the lower grade is never once said to have committed any misdeeds — they are good people, fit only to be the middle grade of the nine grades. He insisted on turning the lower grade into the lower grade
(this is “making trouble out of nothing”)

, contrary to the sutra and lacking in principle — this amounts to altering the sutra at will, and the error is great. In his thinking, the Buddha surely embraces all beings without exception, yet he does not realize that he embraces only the good, not the evil. Since he took good people for evil people, he said they do not give rise to the bodhi mind. Rigidly clinging to the notion that the lower grade is the lower grade, he mistook good people for evil people. He did not realize that the lower three of the nine grades, at the end of life in extreme suffering, upon once hearing the Buddha’s name, have a heart of wholehearted refuge and sincerity, longing for the Buddha’s compassionate rescue, whose brave fervor and gratitude are thousands, ten-thousands of times deeper than the heart of one awaiting execution who hopes for pardon. Although it is not said that they give rise to the bodhi mind, the earnestness and sincerity of their thought in fact fully possess the bodhi mind. It is a pity that Master Wang did not follow the meaning of the original sutra text, but instead relied on the Contemplation Sutra
(the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha)

, forcibly slandering good people as evil people, and judging them as evil. Since Master Wang himself had such a fault, how can later generations presume to pose as authorities? Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble out of nothing?
Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already provides the correct causes of rebirth for the upper, middle, and lower three grades, why make trouble out of nothing and forcibly force them into the
upper three, middle three, and lower three grades
of the nine grades of the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha?
— this is Master Wang’s error.
Please note: throughout this entire letter, Master Yinguang is speaking of Master Wang’s error, not of whether the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may be compiled!
Therefore,
“since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble out of nothing”
— this sentence
must never be distorted into

since the original translation already exists, why make trouble out of nothing by compiling? Moreover, if Master Yinguang’s meaning in saying this had been “since the original translation already exists, why make trouble out of nothing by compiling?” he would surely have said:
since the original translation already exists
, why make trouble out of nothing?”
rather than saying:
since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists
, why make trouble out of nothing?”
because
“the Sutra of Immeasurable Life”
corresponds to
“the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha”
; at the very beginning of this letter, Master Yinguang wrote:
In the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
there are three grades;
in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha
there are nine grades.”
And
what corresponds to
the compiled edition”
should be
“the original translation

Master Wang’s error was pointed out by Master Lianchi, but he had not yet said why it was so. I now explain the reason for it: it is due to rigidly clinging to the notion that the three grades are the nine grades. I write this partly to show
the difficulty of compiling
, and partly to put an end to the presumptions of later generations
that is, on the one hand to put an end to the later generations’ presumptuous clinging to the view that ‘the three grades are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades’
. As for Wei Moshen, there is even less need to speak of him. Bold but crude, he is not fit to serve as a model
(not worthy to be taken as a model)
[Analysis] This teaching of Master Yinguang concerns the problem of the “Wang Compilation”:
“rigidly clinging to the notion that the three grades are the nine grades
(rigidly clinging to the view that the three grades spoken of in the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are the nine grades spoken of in the Contemplation Sutra of Amitāyus Buddha, namely
the upper three, middle three, and lower three grades among them
He never said
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled!
Moreover, Master Yinguang writes at the very end:
“I write this partly to show
the difficulty of compiling
, and partly to put an end to the presumptions of later generations
(in writing the above, I wish on the one hand to show
the difficulty of compiling
, and on the other to put an end to the later generations’ presumptuous clinging to the view that ‘the three grades are the upper three, middle three, and lower three of the nine grades’)
This is to say: the compiling of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life is so difficult that a bold but crude man like Wei Moshen could not be equal to the task, and his method of compiling (
“supplementing it from other sutras
(that is, sutras other than the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
) is even less worthy to serve as a model.
This also
proves
that Master Yinguang held the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could be compiled
, but that it must be done by someone equal to the task. For if Master Yinguang had held that it could not be compiled,
he would have said:
“I write this partly to show
that it cannot be compiled
rather than saying:
“partly to show
the difficulty of compiling
In sum, within these three passages,
Master Yinguang
never said
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could not be compiled!
Rather, he said: a compiled edition must not be circulated as if it were a sutra (that is, when circulating a compiled edition,
one must clearly label it as a compiled edition
), and compiling is a difficult task that must be undertaken by someone equal to it.
Moreover, Master Yinguang’s saying
“I write this partly to show
the difficulty of compiling
— this very sentence
proves:
Master Yinguang was saying that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could be compiled

The compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life promotes the Sutra of Immeasurable Life and helps students steep themselves in it: grasping its meaning, deepening faith and vow, and practicing as taught.
Hence Master Lianchi said of the compiled edition:
“It has rendered great service to the Pure Land.”
Master Ouyi said of the compiled edition:
“This is the wheel of Dharmākara’s vows.”

In his renowned Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, wherever Master Lianchi quotes the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, he for the most part quotes the compiled edition, and only occasionally the original translation.
Master Youxi, in his renowned Commentary on the Perfect Circle of Amitābha, quotes the compiled edition exclusively.
Moreover, Wang Longshu’s compiled edition was examined and approved by eminent monks and included in the Qianlong Tripitaka.
All this shows that
all the eminent monks unanimously approved that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life could be compiled
“This is the wheel of Dharmākara’s vows”
, in order to propagate the Dharma and liberate beings
— great minds think alike.
How could Master Yinguang, a patriarch of his generation, stand outside this? To say that Master Yinguang opposed compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life is truly to have wronged him,
to have plunged the Master into injustice

[[It is truly to have wronged Master Yinguang, to have plunged the Master into injustice] There are three great commentaries on the Amitābha Sutra, all indispensable reference works for later generations who study this sutra and promote the Pure Land: Master Lianchi’s Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, Master Youxi’s Commentary on the Perfect Circle of Amitābha, and Master Ouyi’s Essential Commentary on Amitābha. In his renowned Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, wherever Master Lianchi quotes the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, he for the most part quotes the compiled edition, only occasionally the original translation, and he calls the compiled edition:
“It has rendered great service to the Pure Land.”
Master Youxi, in his renowned Commentary on the Perfect Circle of Amitābha, quotes the compiled edition exclusively. And Master Ouyi
even personally proofread and printed Wang Longshu’s compiled edition, and wrote a preface praising it
“This is the wheel of Dharmākara’s vows.”
These three masters of the Pure Land school, whose insight is transcendent and whose Dharma-eye is round and clear, were always deeply admired by Master Yinguang;
how could his own insight be so deficient as to oppose
these three masters and oppose compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life? Hence we say: to claim that Master Yinguang opposed compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life is truly to have wronged him,
to have plunged the Master into injustice!

Questions and Answers on the Compiled Edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
